kept_issues._normalized_body:
The current Keycloak JavaScript adapter returns a token that you have to manually send on the "Authorization" header on every request. To do this, you would typically require remembering that token in a place accessible by JavaScript (e.g. global variables, sessionStorage).

Instead, Keycloak could return a Set-Cookie header with the token so that the browser would automatically send it in the Cookie header in subsequent requests. This would both be more convenient (no manual token propagation needed) and more secure (using HTTP-only cookies would prevent tokens from being accessible by malicious JavaScript, should a cross-site scripting vulnerability occur).

Keycloak already sends a Set-Cookie header back with a token. However, it has a Path=/realms/ / attribute that prevents the browser from propagating it to other sites, despite being SameSite=None. Additionally, the token is different than the one returned by the JavaScript adapter (it uses a different algorithm), which makes it unusable in some (perhaps all) contexts.

In my particular case, I was trying to configure Eclipse MicroProfile to use cookies (using mp.jwt.token.header=Cookie and mp.jwt.token.cookie=KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY) when I found the aforementioned Keycloak limitations: the cookie never reached the backend, and when manually changing the cookie's path in the browser so that it does, MicroProfile complained that the token should have been signed with "RS256" instead of "HS256".

The current Keycloak JavaScript adapter returns a token that you have to manually send on the "Authorization" header on every request. To do this, you would typically require remembering that token in a place accessible by JavaScript (e.g. global variables, `sessionStorage`).

Instead, Keycloak could return a `Set-Cookie` header with the token so that the browser would automatically send it in the `Cookie` header in subsequent requests. This would both be more convenient (no manual token propagation needed) and more secure (using HTTP-only cookies would prevent tokens from being accessible by malicious JavaScript, should a cross-site scripting vulnerability occur).

Keycloak already sends a `Set-Cookie` header back with a token. However, it has a `Path=/realms/<realm>/` attribute that prevents the browser from propagating it to other sites, despite being `SameSite=None`. Additionally, the token is different than the one returned by the JavaScript adapter (it uses a different algorithm), which makes it unusable in some (perhaps all) contexts.

In my particular case, I was trying to [configure Eclipse MicroProfile to use cookies](https://download.eclipse.org/microprofile/microprofile-jwt-auth-2.0/microprofile-jwt-auth-spec-2.0.html#_jwt_and_http_headers) (using `mp.jwt.token.header=Cookie` and `mp.jwt.token.cookie=KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY`) when I found the aforementioned Keycloak limitations: the cookie never reached the backend, and when manually changing the cookie's path in the browser so that it does, MicroProfile complained that the token should have been signed with "RS256" instead of "HS256".
kept_issues.title: Allow cookie-based token propagation (single-page application)

Description

This feature proposal is to add an SPI provider specific to Traefik, just like there are specific ones for Apache, HAPROXY, and NGINX.

It would support specificities of the header value produced by the PassTLSClientCert middleware containing the client certificate.

 Discussion

A related issue on Traefik repository: 

 Motivation

On the Traefik project, we have seen quite a few community use cases involving Keycloak as an Authorization/Authentication server.

And yet, today, there is no SPI provider implementation specific to Traefik available in Keycloak.
For this reason, some of our users were relying on the NGINX SPI provider, which was unintentionally compatible with the header produced by the PassTLSClientCert middleware in Traefik, which contains the client certificate.

Since v2.9.2, the PassTLSClientCert middleware behavior changed and the client certificate PEM bytes are not URL encoded anymore.

Unfortunately, this new behavior makes the NGINX SPI provider unusable with Traefik v2.9.2+, and constitutes a blocker to upgrade for some users of the Traefik community.

After some investigation, it seems that no available SPI provider that can fit with Traefik v2.9.2+ and that can be an alternative to the NGINX one, so a Traefik dedicated SPI provider is very much needed.

 Details

I'm opening this issue to get approval from the Keycloak maintainers to move forward with opening a PR (which is already ready) with the suggested changes.
kept_issues.body:
### Description

This feature proposal is to add an SPI provider specific to Traefik, just like there are specific ones for Apache, HAPROXY, and NGINX.

It would support specificities of the header value produced by the [PassTLSClientCert middleware](https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/middlewares/http/passtlsclientcert/) containing the client certificate.

### Discussion

A related issue on Traefik repository: https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues/9669

### Motivation

On the Traefik project, we have seen quite a few community use cases involving Keycloak as an Authorization/Authentication server.

And yet, today, there is no SPI provider implementation specific to Traefik available in Keycloak.
For this reason, some of our users were relying on the NGINX SPI provider, which was unintentionally compatible with the header produced by the PassTLSClientCert middleware in Traefik, which contains the client certificate.

Since v2.9.2, the PassTLSClientCert middleware behavior changed and the client certificate PEM bytes are not URL encoded anymore.

Unfortunately, this new behavior makes the NGINX SPI provider unusable with Traefik v2.9.2+, and constitutes a blocker to upgrade for some users of the Traefik community.

After some investigation, it seems that no available SPI provider that can fit with Traefik v2.9.2+ and that can be an alternative to the NGINX one, so a Traefik dedicated SPI provider is very much needed.

### Details

I'm opening this issue to get approval from the Keycloak maintainers to move forward with opening a PR (which is already ready) with the suggested changes.
kept_issues.title: Traefik SPI Provider

kept_issues._normalized_body:
Description

On an IDP details when the Request Refresh Token option is Enabled there should appear an option to Refresh Access Token.
When Refresh Access Token is Enabled and an User logs in through that IDP, while the session is alive, Keycloak should use the requested Refresh Token to refresh the Access Token for that IDP.

 Discussion

 

 Motivation

Some IDPs only allow using requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. For example, Google. The problem is that those access_token are short-lived and there's no way to renew them unless your app goes and retrieves the external IDP tokens. But retrieving the external idp tokens defeats the purpose of the token exchange and requires a client with more permissions than what sometimes would be desirable.

Right now there's really no good solution for this use case as far as I understand and I think this would be a possible solution. Even for IDPs that allow for requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token it would be a better user experience if there Keycloak could handle the access token refreshing and I would just need to exchange access tokens.

Another solution would be to allow for requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token on this types of IDPs (Google, etc.) when the Request Refresh Token is enabled on that IDP.

 Details

I'm not familiar with the code but if manpower is needed I'm open to getting my hands dirty to make this happen. As far as design ideas, it's mostly what I already described.
kept_issues.body:
### Description

On an IDP details when the Request Refresh Token option is Enabled there should appear an option to Refresh Access Token.
When Refresh Access Token is Enabled and an User logs in through that IDP, while the session is alive, Keycloak should use the requested Refresh Token to refresh the Access Token for that IDP.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/15938

### Motivation

Some IDPs only allow using `requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token`. For example, Google. The problem is that those access_token are short-lived and there's no way to renew them unless your app goes and [retrieves the external IDP tokens](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_development/index.html#retrieving-external-idp-tokens). But retrieving the external idp tokens defeats the purpose of the token exchange and requires a client with more permissions than what sometimes would be desirable.

Right now there's really no good solution for this use case as far as I understand and I think this would be a possible solution. Even for IDPs that allow for `requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token` it would be a better user experience if there Keycloak could handle the access token refreshing and I would just need to exchange access tokens.

Another solution would be to allow for `requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token` on this types of IDPs (Google, etc.) when the Request Refresh Token is enabled on that IDP.

### Details

I'm not familiar with the code but if manpower is needed I'm open to getting my hands dirty to make this happen. As far as design ideas, it's mostly what I already described.
kept_issues.title: Automatically Refresh IDP Access Token for Token Exchange

Description

Currently, Keycloak only supports a self-contained token. How about supporting also reference token?

Discussion: 

I have already implemented PoC codes for it the by following the specifications and confirmed that they work well as I expected.

 How to manage the cache holding relationship between a self-contained token and a reference token
 - Keycloak does not hold such the cache by itself. A user of Keycloak who wants to use a reference token needs to prepare the cache. Keycloak only defines I/F with the cache.

 Target tokens
 - an access token and a refresh token returned from Token endpoint (excluding an access token returned in an authorization response by OIDC Hybrid flow).

 Keycloak -> a client - converting a self-contained token to a reference token:
 1. Generating and returning an access/refresh token:
 - Endpoint: Token endpoint
 - Protocol flow: Authorization code flow, Device authorization flow, OIDC Backchannel authentication flow (CIBA)
 2. Re-generating and returning an access/refresh token:
 - Endpoint: Token endpoint
 - Protocol flow: Token refresh

 A client/resource server -> Keycloak - converting a reference token to a self-contained token:
 1. Receiving a token refresh request:
 - Endpoint: Token endpoint
 - Token: a refresh token
 - Protocol flow: Token refresh
 2. Receiving a token introspect request:
 - Endpoint: Token Introspection endpoint
 - Token: an access token, a refresh token
 - Protocol flow: Token introspection
 3. Receiving a UserInfo request:
 - Endpoint: UserInfo endpoint
 - Token: an access token
 - Protocol flow: UserInfo request
 4. Receiving a token revoke request:
 - Endpoint: Token revocation endpoint
 - Token: an access token, a refresh token
 - Protocol flow: Token revoke request
 5. Receiving a backchannel logout (legacy) request:
 - Endpoint: Logout endpoint
 - Token: a refresh token
 - Protocol flow: Backchannel logout (legacy, not OIDC for logout compliant)

 How to convert a self-contained token to a reference token and vise versa:
 - Abstract class of client policies' executor (SPI provider)

 How to generate a reference token
 - Concrete class of client policies' executor (SPI provider), so a user of Keycloak can customize it.

 How to define and implement I/F an external cache holding relationship between a self-contained token and a reference token:
 - Concrete class of client policies' executor (SPI provider), so a user of Keycloak can customize it.

 Actual reference implementation of such the I/F with the cache:
 - I/F: REST API
 - bind and store the relationship between a self-contained token and a reference token
 - Request (application/json): a reference token, a self-contained token
 - Method: POST
 - Response
 - 204 No Content
 - 400 Bad Request
 - 500 Internal Server Error
 - get the self-contained token bound with the reference token
 - Request: the reference token
 - Method: GET
 - Response (application/json)
 - 200 OK: the self-contained token
 - 400 Bad Request
 - 500 Internal Server Error

 Actual reference implementation of a reference token
 - Format: "jti" claim value of a self-contained token

 Discussion

 

 Motivation

 - Privacy: Some use cases require not including sensitive data like Personal Identifiable Information (PII) in an access token.
 - Confidentiality: Not disclosing information which a resource server only need to know to 3rd party entities like clients.
 - Security requirement: Some use cases requires a reference token as their requirement.

 Details

 - Cache: Keycloak does not implement such the cache by itself. Instead of it, Keycloak defines I/F with the cache and a user of Keycloak prepares it implementing the I/F, which burdens a user of Keycloak who want to use a reference token. However, Keycloak itself and other user who uses a self-contained token as usual are not affected by supporting a reference token.
 - Non-invasive way: a reference token is realized by client policies, which means that Keycloak's body codes and other user who uses a self-contained token as usual are not affected by supporting a reference token.
 - Flexibility: by using client policies, it is easy to specify which clients use a reference token. Namely, we can select using a reference token or a self-contained token per client.
 - Flexibility: a user of Keycloak can implement their own I/F with the cache as a SPI provider.

kept_issues._normalized_body:
The Operator currently creates passthrough Routes by default (if TLS is not configured, unlike Nginx Ingress that uses uses a reencrypt strategy. Passthrough has (among others) performance implications on Keycloak.

We should either make reencrypt the default strategy, or make it configurable (affecting both Routes and Nginx Ingress).

Considerations
 This is potentially a breaking change.
 reencrypt requires configuring the Route to trust the Keycloak's certificate. This might be a bit tricky doing manually and not something we want to force the users to do. Keycloak should be automatically configured to use TLS key/cert that is generated by OpenShift CA (and therefore implicitly trusted by the Routes).

Workaround
Disable the default Ingress and create a custom Route.
kept_issues.body:
The Operator currently creates `passthrough` Routes by default (if TLS is not configured, unlike Nginx Ingress that uses uses a reencrypt strategy. Passthrough has (among others) performance implications on Keycloak.

We should either make `reencrypt` the default strategy, or make it configurable (affecting both Routes and Nginx Ingress).

**Considerations**
* This is potentially a breaking change.
* `reencrypt` requires configuring the Route to trust the Keycloak's certificate. This might be a bit tricky doing manually and not something we want to force the users to do. Keycloak should be automatically configured to use TLS key/cert that is generated by OpenShift CA (and therefore implicitly trusted by the Routes).

**Workaround**
Disable the default Ingress and create a custom Route.
kept_issues.title: Add support for `reencrypt` OpenShift Routes to the Operator

kept_issues.body:
### Description

Caddy is a relatively new web server. To support Caddy as a reverse proxy provider for client certificate authentication, the Keycloak team will need to add support for Base64-encoded DER certificates. As of right now, Keycloak only supports PEM files.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

While Caddy is a new web server, it is not uncommon. Caddy has been used by Cloudflare in their implementation of their MITM protection service; separately, Let's Encrypt considers Caddy's "implementation of [ACME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_Certificate_Management_Environment) to be the gold standard of ACME clients," per [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddy_(web_server)). Supporting Caddy would be a great addition to Keycloak as more enterprises consider Caddy for their web server needs.

### Details

Per the [lead developer](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/3767#issuecomment-1574294070), Caddy will not support passing PEM-formatted certificates in HTTP headers, and instead only supports B64-encoded DERs; therefore, the standard Apache, Nginx and HAProxy provider options do not work with Caddy. Caddy also does not automatically construct a certificate chain when passing a client certificate, similar to how Nginx currently works (Keycloak documentation mentions this [here](https://www.keycloak.org/server/reverseproxy) under "Configuring the NGINX provider").

My ask is to add Caddy as a reverse proxy provider. This would be nearly identical to the Nginx provider, except Keycloak must accept B64'ed DER certificates. As of right now, if a DER certificate is passed to Keycloak via Caddy, the following error occurs, as the format lacks the expected new line characters:

```
ERROR [org.keycloak.services] (executor-thread-50) org.keycloak.common.util.PemException: org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.x509.CertificateFactory$ExCertificateException: parsing issue: 
long form definite-length more than 31 bits: java.security.GeneralSecurityException: org.keycloak.common.util.PemException: org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.x509.CertificateFactory$ExCertificateException: parsing issue: long fo
rm definite-length more than 31 bits
```
kept_issues.title: Support Caddy as a Reverse Proxy Provider for Client Certificate Authentication

Keycloak server can support configuration and customization for the Hibernate Naming Strategy configuration.

 Discussion

N/A

 Motivation

Since the users can use a non empty database schema for persistent JPA storage, the tables created by Keycloak may conflict with exisiting schema.
The feature can be used to add prefixes to entities to be added in the database.

 Details

The feature can be added as an extension to JPA service provider for supporting the required configuration or the DefaultJpaConnectionProviderFactory can be updated to accept the configuration for Hibernate. 
The feature can only support the physical naming strategy, since Keycloak entities are defined with @Table(name=" ") annotation with explicit names, hence the support for implicit naming configuration is redundant.
kept_issues.body:
### Description

Keycloak server can support configuration and customization for the Hibernate Naming Strategy configuration.

### Discussion

N/A

### Motivation

Since the users can use a non empty database schema for persistent JPA storage, the tables created by Keycloak may conflict with exisiting schema.
The feature can be used to add prefixes to entities to be added in the database.

### Details

The feature can be added as an extension to JPA service provider for supporting the required configuration or the DefaultJpaConnectionProviderFactory can be updated to accept the configuration for Hibernate. 
The feature can only support the [physical naming strategy](https://docs.jboss.org/hibernate/orm/5.0/userguide/html_single/Hibernate_User_Guide.html#PhysicalNamingStrategy), since Keycloak entities are defined with [`@Table(name="<name>")`](https://docs.oracle.com/javaee/7/api/javax/persistence/Table.html) annotation with explicit names, hence the support for implicit naming configuration is redundant.
kept_issues.title: Keycloak does not support Hibernate naming strategy

Description

The OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 spec suggests that a logout_hint parameter can be used instead of the id_token_hint.

We would like to contribute support for _logout_hint_ for the OIDC Identity Provider.

 Discussion

_No response_

 Motivation

Sometimes the ID token of an Identity Provider contains so much data, that the logout url - containing the ID Token as id_token_hint parameter - becomes too large to be handled by some browsers/servers.

We have faced this issue with Azure AD, where some of our customers have lots of roles or groups defined. Limiting the token by filtering the roles/groups is not an option for some of the customers, because most of them are relevant for their applications.

To circumvent logout failures, we have implemented a custom OIDC Identity Provider which supports the logout_hint feature supported by Azure AD.

 Details

It is not specified in the spec, which value this logout_hint should contain. Azure AD requires a special claim named login_hint (not to be confused with the parameter of the same name, which can be used for OIDC login), see 

Probably it makes sense to support a flexible configuration for the OIDC Identity Provider implementation. It could be configurable whether id_token_hint or logout_hint should be used for logout. When logout_hint is selected, the key of an ID token claim could be specified, which provides the value to be used for logout. For Azure AD, this would be login_hint. For Auth0, it would be sid (see 

WDYT of supporting the logout_hint parameter?
kept_issues.body:
### Description

The [OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 spec](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-rpinitiated-1_0.html#RPLogout) suggests that a `logout_hint` parameter can be used instead of the `id_token_hint`.

We would like to contribute support for _logout_hint_ for the OIDC Identity Provider.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Sometimes the ID token of an Identity Provider contains so much data, that the logout url - containing the ID Token as `id_token_hint` parameter - becomes too large to be handled by some browsers/servers.

We have faced this issue with Azure AD, where some of our customers have lots of roles or groups defined. Limiting the token by filtering the roles/groups is not an option for some of the customers, because most of them are relevant for their applications.

To circumvent logout failures, we have implemented a custom OIDC Identity Provider which supports the `logout_hint` feature supported by Azure AD.

### Details

It is not specified in the spec, which value this `logout_hint` should contain. Azure AD requires a special claim named `login_hint` (not to be confused with the parameter of the same name, which can be used for OIDC login), see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/v2-protocols-oidc#send-a-sign-out-request.

Probably it makes sense to support a flexible configuration for the OIDC Identity Provider implementation. It could be configurable whether `id_token_hint` or `logout_hint` should be used for logout. When `logout_hint` is selected, the key of an ID token claim could be specified, which provides the value to be used for logout. For Azure AD, this would be `login_hint`.  For Auth0, it would be `sid` (see https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/logout/log-users-out-of-auth0).

WDYT of  supporting the `logout_hint` parameter?
kept_issues.title: OIDC Identity Provider: Support logout_hint as an alternative to id_token_hint for OIDC logout

Description

I want to use Keycloak on OpenShift (OCP) and want to make sure there is Route created for Keycloak, even if I had not specified upfront the hostname value for Keycloak to use.

Seems that Keycloak operator assumes that Route for Keycloak is auto-generated by OpenShift based on the Ingress resource creates, granted one specifies className: openshift-default in the Keycloak CR. And then, when if there is Keycloak.spec.hostname specified, adds the host into Ingress resource created.

However, on OCP 4.12+, route-controller-manager creates Route based on the Ingress resource, ONLY if the Ingress resource has .spec.rules.host specified, otherwise no Route is created.

It is perfectly valid to create Route on OpenShift, without host being specified - in such case, OCP auto-generated the host in the .apps. subdomain.

So, my key questions are:
- Is the assumption that hostname is specified in Keycloak CR correct - i.e. is this parameter absolutely required for Keycloak application to work correctly?
 - what breaks when hostname is not specified in Keycloak CR?
- If hostname parameter is not required, should we have the updated Keycloak operator logic in the appropriate way, so that Route is created on OpenShift (perhaps a strict tie to Ingres->Route autogeneration could be revised?)

A bit related discussion: , since eventually we'd like to use the re-encrypt Routes, with the certifies being rotated and replaced with customer's certificates.

 Discussion

_No response_

 Motivation

Using Keyclok on OpenShift requires Route to be exposed outside of the cluster, for external applications / processes interactions.

 Details

_No response_
kept_issues.body:
### Description

I want to use Keycloak on OpenShift (OCP) and want to make sure there is `Route` created for Keycloak, even if I had not specified upfront the hostname value for Keycloak to use.

Seems that Keycloak operator assumes that `Route` for Keycloak is auto-generated by OpenShift based on the `Ingress` resource creates, granted one specifies `className: openshift-default` in the `Keycloak` CR. And then, when if there is `Keycloak.spec.hostname` specified, [adds](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/controllers/KeycloakIngress.java#L111) the `host` into `Ingress` resource created.


However, on OCP 4.12+, [`route-controller-manager`](https://github.com/openshift/route-controller-manager) creates `Route` based on the `Ingress` resource, [ONLY if the `Ingress` resource has `.spec.rules.host` specified](https://github.com/openshift/route-controller-manager/blob/main/pkg/route/ingress/ingress.go#L416), otherwise no `Route` is created.

It is perfectly valid to create `Route` on OpenShift, without `host` being specified - in such case, OCP auto-generated the host in the `*.apps.<cluster-dns-name>` subdomain.

So, my key questions are:
- Is the assumption that `hostname` is specified in `Keycloak` CR correct - i.e. is this parameter absolutely required for Keycloak application to work correctly?
  - what breaks when `hostname` is not specified in `Keycloak` CR?
- If `hostname` parameter is not required, should we have the updated Keycloak operator logic in the appropriate way, so that `Route` is created on OpenShift (perhaps a strict tie to Ingres->Route autogeneration could be revised?)

A bit related discussion: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/20128 , since eventually we'd like to use the re-encrypt Routes, with the certifies being rotated and replaced with customer's certificates.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Using Keyclok on OpenShift requires `Route` to be exposed outside of the cluster, for external applications / processes interactions.

### Details

_No response_
kept_issues.title: Have Route created on OCP even when no Keycloak CR hostname specified

- Enhanced Event-Driven Architecture: Organizations can benefit from event-driven architecture, enabling responsive and scalable identity and access management.

- Reduced Custom Development: Users would no longer need to build custom middleware to connect Keycloak with message brokers, saving time and effort.

kept_issues.body:
As part of implementing the Federated Credential Management API (see #16834), we will have to extend the REST API with new endpoints and fields to support it.

Ideally we would have a separate 'protocol' specifically for FedCM, for example:

- `https://keycloak.org/realms/master/protocol/fed-cm`

Until the specification and our implementation is considered stable we'll have to put this functionality behind [a profile](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/63fc38ca1f0db9d9774ad9a8f50bb9cc8f7a4d13/common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/Profile.java#L41) (e.g. `Profile.FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL_MANAGEMENT`).

For this we'll need the following:

### A well-known file

- Can we do this on per realm basis, or does it need to be in the root?

For more information see the developer documentation: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/privacy-sandbox/fedcm-developer-guide/#well-known-file


### An endpoint for the config file

- For now let's only implement required fields (TODO, create an issue for the optional ones)

For more information see the developer documentation: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/privacy-sandbox/fedcm-developer-guide/#idp-config-file

### An endpoint for the accounts list

- In Keycloak the e-mail of a user is not required, so we'll likely have to filter those users out.
- For `approved_clients` we can probably return all clients in a realm (TODO find out if this can be restricted).

For more information see the developer documentation: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/privacy-sandbox/fedcm-developer-guide/#accounts-list-endpoint

### An endpoint for ID assertion

- Let's skip the `nonce` for now (TODO create an issue to do this later)

For more information see the developer documentation: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/privacy-sandbox/fedcm-developer-guide/#id-assertion-endpoint
kept_issues.title: Extend the REST API for FedCM

origin validation may fail for non-Web platforms

for example:

- Android:
  - `android:apk-key-hash-sha256:<base64_encoded_sha256_hash-of-apk-signing-cert>`

kept_issues.body:
### Description

Introduce a new SPI for CORS and create a default implementation based on `org.keycloak.services.resources.Cors`.

### Discussion

_(discussed at 6th OAuth SIG)_

### Motivation

Currently, we have `Cors` class that belongs to `services` and is not visible from other modules. The behavior is mostly hardcoded with limited configurability. The introduction of CORS SPI will help solve the following issues:
* Expose the `Cors` class to the provider infrastructure. Currently, one can only pass `Cors` to a provider as `java.lang.Object` and then cast it back in the implementation ([1](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenExchangeContext.java#L43), [2](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/DefaultTokenExchangeProvider.java#L120)). This will also be required by the upcoming OAuth 2.0 Grant SPI;
* The default implementation will have its configuration namespace (`kc.spi-cors-default`) which will allow to customize the behavior (example: #12682)
* The SPI will allow to replace the built-in CORS implementation with a custom one if needed.

### Details

As long as CORS implementation is going to be a provider, using it will require a `KeycloakSession`. At the OAuth SIG, we have agreed that we can have a new session-based API whilst (temporarily) keeping the old one:
```java
// old API
Cors cors = Cors.add(request);
Cors cors = Cors.add(request, response);

// new API
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class); // request object will be obtained from KeycloakContext, should cover the absolute majority of cases
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class).request(request); // override request object
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class).builder(builder); // set builder
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class).request(request).builder(builder); // override both, should be rare
```

This will result in the following changes/decisions:
* The `org.keycloak.common.util.Resteasy` class will need to be moved to the `common` module, otherwise it won't be accessible from the `Cors::add` methods (which will need to resolve `KeycloakSession` via a Resteasy context).
kept_issues.title: CORS SPI

Description

Since MapStorageSpi and MAP_STORAGE-feature have been removed, it became quite challenging to replace Keycloak storage including Infinispan-caching with a custom implementation. I understand that supporting something like map store was too big in scope and very challenging for the core team. Thus i am proposing a kind of middle ground: A CustomDatastore-feature which disables all of the default storage providers to simplify replacing them with custom implementations.

If you support this idea, i could provide the implementation.

 Discussion

 

 Motivation

Right now, to replace default datastore one not only has to implement DatastoreProvider but also needs to make sure that default implementations are not loaded (as they register themselves as event listeners, start infinispan-caches, do JPA-database migrations, etc inside of init()).
This was taken care of in KC < 23 when Feature.MAP_STORAGE was enabled, as all "Legacy"-providers where then disabled via EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory.isSupported().

This is no longer the case in KC 23. Thus to achieve the same we did not find another way than either disabling all the default providers (cumbersome) or overriding them by using the same ID and a higher order() (weird).
And currently there is no way at all to disable JPA/Cache Quarkus-BuildSteps.

 Details

- Add a CUSTOM_DATASTORE-feature (experimental)
- If this feature is activated, all default storage providers are deactivated via EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory (basically replace all occurences of !Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.MAP_STORAGE) from KC < 23 with !Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.CUSTOM_DATASTORE)
- Introduce IsCustomDatastoreEnabled BooleanSupplier (based on IsLegacyStoreEnabled from KC < 23) to disable Cache- and JPA-Quarkus-BuildSteps

### Description

Since `MapStorageSpi` and `MAP_STORAGE`-feature have been removed, it became quite challenging to replace Keycloak storage including Infinispan-caching with a custom implementation. I understand that supporting something like map store was too big in scope and very challenging for the core team. Thus i am proposing a kind of middle ground: A CustomDatastore-feature which disables all of the default storage providers to simplify replacing them with custom implementations.

If you support this idea, i could provide the implementation.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/24052

### Motivation

Right now, to replace default datastore one not only has to implement `DatastoreProvider` but also needs to make sure that default implementations are not loaded (as they register themselves as event listeners, start infinispan-caches, do JPA-database migrations, etc inside of `init()`).
This was taken care of in KC < 23 when `Feature.MAP_STORAGE` was enabled, as all "Legacy"-providers where then disabled via `EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory.isSupported()`.

This is no longer the case in KC 23. Thus to achieve the same we did not find another way than either disabling all the default providers (cumbersome) or overriding them by using the same ID and a higher `order()` (weird).
And currently there is no way at all to disable JPA/Cache Quarkus-BuildSteps.

### Details

- Add a `CUSTOM_DATASTORE`-feature (experimental)
- If this feature is activated, all default storage providers are deactivated via `EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory` (basically replace all occurences of `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.MAP_STORAGE)` from KC < 23 with `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.CUSTOM_DATASTORE)`
- Introduce `IsCustomDatastoreEnabled` BooleanSupplier (based on `IsLegacyStoreEnabled` from KC < 23) to disable Cache- and JPA-Quarkus-BuildSteps

### Description

The protocol is intended to offer and issue credentials to wallets in a secure and standard way. 


### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions?discussions_q=is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%2Foid4vc

### Motivation

OID4VCI seems to be the most mature and used issuance protocol at the moment. Its already used and mandated by various projects:

* [EBSI](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/display/EBSI)

* [DSBA Technical Convergence](https://data-spaces-business-alliance.eu/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Data-Spaces-Business-Alliance-Technical-Convergence-V2.pdf)

Implementing wallets can for example be found at the [EBSI conformant wallets](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/display/EBSI/Conformant+wallets).

### Details

https://github.com/francis-pouatcha/keycloak-community/blob/OIDC4VCI-Design-2/design/OID4VCI.md

kept_issues.body:
### Description

Split from the PR of #20677 and the origin issue is #9209 

Need to introduce a new Authenticator to handle duplicate IdP broker links when first login flow, 
which will show some confirmation screen then overriding the broker link would be possible.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/20677

### Motivation

There are two cases when updating the broker link when duplicates exists.
case 1:
```
[before]
User A:
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: user_a
     - user_id: id_1

when the new broker_link comes
(This happens when the broker_user create a new account but use the previous username)
broker_user:
    - username: user_a
    - user_id: id_2

[after]
User A:
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: user_a
     - user_id: id_2
 ```

case 2:
```
[before]
User A:
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: whatever
     - user_id: id_1

when the new broker_link comes
(This happens when the broker_user just changed its username)
broker_user:
    - username: user_b
    - user_id: id_1

[after]
User A
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: user_b
     - user_id: id_1
 ```
The case 2 makes sure the ID not changed.


### Details

For the case 1 with security concern,

> we should introduce a step during the flow to say "Hey, looks like you have an existing account linked to Foo IdP but using a different than the account you are now authenticating. Do you confirm using the new account instead?"

And make sure the user confirm the override existing broker link.

Introduce a new Authenticator for the first login flow, the process might be:

1. try find the user by `identityProvider` and `brokerUsername`
2. display a confirm screen if exists
3. verify the email by code if user has email (by IdpEmailVerificationAuthenticator)
4. otherwise, we can verify by the credential (by IdpUsernamePasswordForm)
kept_issues.title: Introduce a new Authenticator to handle duplicate IdP broker links

- Simplify adding new grant types (e.g. pre-authorized_code for OID4VCI);
- Support OAuth 2.0 Extension Grants.

### Description

When running the container for development purposes it starts fairly slowly. It would be nice to have a dev optimized container that starts as fast as possible.

As an example the following container will use local caches, initialize the DB, and do an optimized build:
```
FROM quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:23.0.6 as builder

ENV KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=admin
ENV KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin

RUN /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh build --cache=local
RUN /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh export --file /tmp/export.json

FROM quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:23.0.6
COPY --from=builder /opt/keycloak/ /opt/keycloak/

ENV KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=admin
ENV KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin

ENV KC_HTTP_ENABLED=true
ENV KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh"]
```

The above container starts on my box in 2.9s, while the default container with `start-dev` starts in 2.6s (for auto-build) + 5.4s (for start-dev). That's almost 1/3 of the startup time.

The dev container should be built as part of the release, and either added to `keycloak/keycloak-dev` or perhaps just a tag like `keycloak/keycloak:dev`.

Some improvements could be made to the above for example:

Description

This feature request asks to add support for configurable properties to RequiredActions. 
Currently support for configuration of required actions via the admin ui are quite limited. 
The only allowed configuration options are: 
- enabled (is the required action enabled at all?)
- default (is the required action set for new users by default?) 
- order / priority (controls the order in which required actions is presented to the user)

It would be helpful to allow developers to specify additional configurable properties org.keycloak.provider.ProviderConfigProperty for required actions, similar to how authenticator executions can be configured.

 Discussion

_No response_

 Motivation

Behaviour for required actions should be configurable. Currently one has to pull configuration from realm attributes, env variables or other means.
Having official support for configuration would allow us to have a common way to configure actions. 

 Details

 Implementation ideas

 Configuration options 

There are multiple ways to implement support for configuration options for required actions, here are 2 options:

 Option 1
Leverage org.keycloak.provider.ProviderFactorygetConfigMetadata()
Advantages:
- easier, as it is already available API

Disadvantages:
- no default config 
- no help text 

 Option 2
Make required actions infrastructure aware of org.keycloak.provider.ConfiguredProvider 
Advantages:
- more options (help text, default config) 
- Developers could opt-in to make their required actions configurable by implementing the ConfiguredProvider interface.

Disadvantages:
- a bit more work
- 2 different ways to define config properties (ProviderFactorygetConfigMetadata() vs. ConfiguredProvidergetConfigProperties()) 

I currently lean toward Option 1.

 Required Action Configuration storage

The required actions infrastructure already supports the persistence of configuration metadata via 
org.keycloak.models.jpa.entities.RequiredActionProviderEntityconfig in the REQUIRED_ACTION_CONFIG table.

 REST API extensions in AuthenticationManagementResource 

The AuthenticationManagementResource already supports the management of required actions. It seems as the natural place to add support for required action config management.

I propose to add the following new endpoints to manage required action configuration within a realm bound to the required action "alias" / provider id.
 

 Additional work
- Introduce RequiredActionConfigModel
- Extend RequiredActionContext to expose RequiredActionConfigModel
- Extend admin-client libraries (jakarta, javaee, js/ts)
- Extend admin ui (required action list with config button and required action config form)
- Update documentation
- Update tests (REST API, UI tests)
kept_issues.body:
### Description

This feature request asks to add support for configurable properties to RequiredActions. 
Currently support for configuration of required actions via the admin ui are quite limited. 
The only allowed configuration options are: 
- enabled (is the required action enabled at all?)
- default (is the required action set for new users by default?) 
- order / priority (controls the order in which required actions is presented to the user)

It would be helpful to allow developers to specify additional configurable properties `org.keycloak.provider.ProviderConfigProperty` for required actions, similar to how authenticator executions can be configured.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Behaviour for required actions should be configurable. Currently one has to pull configuration from realm attributes, env variables or other means.
Having official support for configuration would allow us to have a common way to configure actions. 

### Details

# Implementation ideas

## Configuration options 

There are multiple ways to implement support for configuration options for required actions, here are 2 options:

### Option 1
Leverage `org.keycloak.provider.ProviderFactory#getConfigMetadata()`
Advantages:
- easier, as it is already available API

Disadvantages:
- no default config 
- no help text 

### Option 2
Make required actions infrastructure aware of `org.keycloak.provider.ConfiguredProvider` 
Advantages:
- more options (help text, default config) 
- Developers could opt-in to make their required actions configurable by implementing the `ConfiguredProvider` interface.

Disadvantages:
- a bit more work
- 2 different ways to define config properties (`ProviderFactory#getConfigMetadata()` vs. `ConfiguredProvider#getConfigProperties()`) 

I currently lean toward Option 1.

## Required Action Configuration storage

The required actions infrastructure already supports the persistence of configuration metadata via 
[`org.keycloak.models.jpa.entities.RequiredActionProviderEntity#config`](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/entities/RequiredActionProviderEntity.java#L76) in the `REQUIRED_ACTION_CONFIG` table.

## REST API extensions in AuthenticationManagementResource 

The `AuthenticationManagementResource` already supports the management of required actions. It seems as the natural place to add support for required action config management.

I propose to add the following new endpoints to manage required action configuration within a realm bound to the required action "alias" / provider id.
```
  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config-description")
  @GET
  @Produces(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
  RequiredActionConfigInfoRepresentation getRequiredActionConfigDescription(@PathParam("alias") String alias);

  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config")
  @GET
  @Produces(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
  RequiredActionConfigRepresentation getRequiredActionConfig(@PathParam("alias") String alias);

  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config")
  @DELETE
  void removeRequiredActionConfig(@PathParam("alias") String alias);

  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config")
  @PUT
  @Consumes(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
  void updateRequiredActionConfig(@PathParam("alias") String alias, RequiredActionConfigRepresentation rep);
```

## Additional work
- Introduce RequiredActionConfigModel
- Extend RequiredActionContext to expose RequiredActionConfigModel
- Extend admin-client libraries (jakarta, javaee, js/ts)
- Extend admin ui (required action list with config button and required action config form)
- Update documentation
- Update tests (REST API, UI tests)

Description

Inviting users would be a very useful feature that is currently not supported by keycloak or any extension (I didn't find any). 

Flow:
- The admin creates a user in the keycloak admin portal, where the minimum is an email address (may include other data - first name, last name,...) without a password, and sets the user required action 'invite user'. It can also do this via api request on keycloak.
- The new user receives an email entered by the administrator with a link to the page where he completes the missing data (which fields should be displayed can be configured - also possible in later versions). of course, the password field is mandatory. The link has a default validity period of 1 week (the admin can change it in the admin console).
- If a new user fills in the missing information with a password in time, the appropriate flag is set for him that he is registered (with the aim of distinguishing truly registered users from those invited who have not yet responded to the invitation).
- If the user does not use the link in time, when clicking on the expired link, he receives a notification that he should again ask the administrator for a new link, without which he cannot complete the registration.
- The administrator can also see the list of all invited users (also via the keycloak api) and the status of whether the link has expired. He can then decide whether to delete the user or send the invitation again (both actions can also be triggered using the keycloak api). 
- Administrator can also set in the admin settings console that the new user template is automatically removed from the database after the invite link expires.

 Discussion

_No response_

 Motivation

I believe that inviting new users would be a very welcome functionality especially in the case of enterprise users.

 Details

Based on the design as specified in 9829.

Add a new command: kc.sh|bat bootstrap-admin user [--username=value] [--password=value] [--no-prompt] [--expiration=value].
 The command works regardless if Keycloak was ever started (and master realm exists), or not.
 If --username is not specified, the env variable KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted to enter a username with a default preset to temp-admin.
 If --password is not specified, the environment variable KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted for a password.
 If --no-prompt is specified, then prompting will not be used. If a value would have required prompting, an error will be shown.
 If the account with the specified username exists an error will be shown.
 --expiration specifies the number of minutes after which the account expires. If --expiration is not specified, the environment variable KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EXPIRATION will be checked. Otherwise, the default 120 (2 hours) will be used.
kept_issues.body:
Based on the design as specified in #9829.

Add a new command: `kc.sh|bat bootstrap-admin user [--username=value] [--password=value] [--no-prompt] [--expiration=value]`.
* The command works regardless if Keycloak was ever started (and master realm exists), or not.
* If `--username` is not specified, the env variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME` will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted to enter a username with a default preset to `temp-admin`.
* If `--password` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted for a password.
* If `--no-prompt` is specified, then prompting will not be used. If a value would have required prompting, an error will be shown.
* If the account with the specified username exists an error will be shown.
* `--expiration` specifies the number of minutes after which the account expires. If `--expiration` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EXPIRATION` will be checked. Otherwise, the default `120` (2 hours) will be used.

 Short lived (5 minutes)
 One time use only

Drawbacks:

 Would have the same issues as import / export wrt - 
 Not great usability when containerized - probably need a cr driven mechanism for triggering the creation of the token, which would then be available via a Secret.

### Description

The default discovery protocol provided by Infinispan uses IP multicast (`MPING`) to find its peers in the network. Although it is perfectly fine for an environment with IP multicast available, `JDBC_PING2` seems a better fit as a default discovery protocol for Keycloak. 

The `JDBC_PING2` protocol uses a database to keep track of the peer's IP addresses (and ports) and, we can use the Keycloak database as a registry.

The following work is required:

* Create a custom stack, replacing `MPING` with `JDBC_PING2`
* Infinispan 15.0.3.Final allows injecting a data source into `JDBC_PING2` for Infinispan Server (see https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ISPN-15961). The same code can be used by Keycloak to inject the Quarkus data source into JGroups.
* (UX improvement) Somehow detect the database dialect to configure the `JDBC_PING2` queries (select, delete, insert). The goal is to achieve zero-config for users.
* Set values for remaining options based on user feedback and/or issues found.

`JDBC_PING2` documentation is available here: http://jgroups.org/manual5/index.html#JDBC_PING2

### Discussion

To simplify Keycloak usage and configuration.

As Keycloak seeks to complete the incubating onboarding items, it must align with the CNCF license policy, which mandates board approval for non-Apache 2.0 dependencies.

To resolve potential license compliance issues, modify future Keycloak community releases to exclude the Oracle driver, requiring it to be installed separately by users. This practice helps address licensing concerns. Note that this change is not applicable to past releases.

2. Update installation guides to include instructions for users on how to install the Oracle driver manually.
3. Adjust the build process to exclude the Oracle driver from all future community releases.
4. Communicate this change to the community, highlighting the reasons related to licensing compliance.

### Description

This task is about support passkeys in the username/password form. The GIF in the attached discussion shows what should be the ideal experience for the end user.

### Implementation notes

In the issue https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/24264 it addressed "proposal 2" and introduced new authenticator for passkeys support with just username field.

This task is about make it possible to integrate with username/password screen. Few possibilities how to address this:

1) Investigate if `FormActionSPI` can be used? This SPI is currently used for registration form. It allows to render single form (like registration form), but have separate "form actions" attached to it. If we go this path, we can have something like this in the configuration of authentication flow to address the use-case like "allow to authenticate user with conditional passkey OR with password":
```
- Username Password Form REQUIRED
  - Passkeys action      ALTERNATIVE
  - Password             ALTERNATIVE
```

2) Add something directly into `UsernamePasswordForm`. I rather vote against it to avoid mixing username/password related logic with WebAuthn/passkeys logic.

3) Introduce separate authenticator (something like `PasskeysUsernamePasswordForm` ?), which would be probably subclass of `UsernamePasswordForm` and may have some additional capabilities related to passkeys. This path may involve update `UsernamePasswordForm` as well (so it is possible to easily extend from it), but `UsernamePasswordForm` should not have any WebAuthn/passkeys logic in itself


My vote of preferred approaches is 1, 3, 2 ATM

kept_issues.body:
### Description

Based on the design as specified in https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/9829.

Add a new command: `kc.sh|bat bootstrap-admin service [--client-id=value] [--secret=value] [--no-prompt] [--expiration=value]`.
* The command works regardless if Keycloak was ever started (and master realm exists), or not.
* If `--client-id` is not specified, the env variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID` will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted to enter a Client ID with a default preset to `temp-admin-service`.
* If `--secret` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET` will be checked, if not defined, the user will be prompted for a secret.
* If `--no-prompt` is specified, then prompting will not be used. If a value would have required prompting, an error will be shown.
* If the Client with the specified Client ID exists an error will be shown.
* `--expiration` specifies the number of minutes after which the Client expires. If `--expiration` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EXPIRATION` will be checked. Otherwise, the default `120` (2 hours) will be used.

Based on the provided arguments, a Client is created in the master Realm with the following specifications:
* It has all flows disabled.
* The Client requires authentication.
* Service account is enabled.
* The service account has the admin Realm Role assigned.

Description

Keycloak should provide the option to configure an MFA option during the first login if all MFA options are set to "Alternative" and no MFA option is configured, instead of failing the login flow. For reference, the following flow fails if the user does not have an MFA option configured:
 

 Discussion

 

 Motivation

Currently Keycloak supports having alternative MFA options (e.g., OTP and WebAuthn), but as far as I can tell there is no support to allow configuring one of the options on the first login. A workaround, mentioned in the linked discussion is to have one of the MFA options as a "Required" step in an "Alternative" subflow, e.g.:
 

In this case, users are presented with the first configured MFA option from the alternatives, and if no MFA token is configured, they are asked to configure an OTP. While this approach works, it does not provide the option to configure the WebAuthn token as the first (and maybe only) token.

 Details

Authentication steps that can be configured (e.g., HOTP / TOTP, WebAuthn, email OTP?) should provide the option to set them up on the first login, so users can configure the token and proceed with the login afterwards, instead of failing the login flow.

The administration console should provide the option to configure the steps as "can be set up as first token", since not all options may be equally applicable for all users (e.g., we can assume users have a computer or phone they can use to generate TOTPs, but FIDO tokens are rather expensive, so they are only used by a small subset of users); if some of the options are not configurable as the first token, they should be available in the account console, but not on the first login screen.
kept_issues.body:
### Description

Keycloak should provide the option to configure an MFA option during the first login if all MFA options are set to "Alternative" and no MFA option is configured, instead of failing the login flow. For reference, the following flow fails if the user does not have an MFA option configured:
```
- Username and password (required)
- MFA (required subflow)
  - OTP Form (alternative)
  - WebAuthn Authenticator (alternative)
```

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/14988

### Motivation

Currently Keycloak supports having alternative MFA options (e.g., OTP and WebAuthn), but as far as I can tell there is no support to allow configuring one of the options on the first login. A workaround, mentioned in the linked discussion is to have one of the MFA options as a "Required" step in an "Alternative" subflow, e.g.:
```
- MFA (required subflow)
  - TOTP (alternative subflow)
    - OTP Form (required)
  - WebAuthn Authenticator (alternative)
```

In this case, users are presented with the first configured MFA option from the alternatives, and if no MFA token is configured, they are asked to configure an OTP. While this approach works, it does not provide the option to configure the WebAuthn token as the first (and maybe only) token.

### Details

Authentication steps that can be configured (e.g., HOTP / TOTP, WebAuthn, email OTP?) should provide the option to set them up on the first login, so users can configure the token and proceed with the login afterwards, instead of failing the login flow.

The administration console should provide the option to configure the steps as "can be set up as first token", since not all options may be equally applicable for all users (e.g., we can assume users have a computer or phone they can use to generate TOTPs, but FIDO tokens are rather expensive, so they are only used by a small subset of users); if some of the options are not configurable as the first token, they should be available in the account console, but not on the first login screen.

Description

Since Keycloak is not yet supporting Rich Authorization Request (RAR), we are using a custom protocol mapper in order to include authorization_details in issued tokens, when using a Pushed Authorization Request (PAR) flow. This was also recommended in discussions/22991.
This is possible because the ParEndpoint processing goes through AuthorizationEndpoint.javaL332, that stores any additional request parameters in client session notes, which can then be accessed from a custom protocol mapper.

However, we also need RAR for a client grant type token. But since the TokenEndpoint processing does not store the additional request parameters, we cannot use the custom protocol mapper to achieve RAR in this case.

Therefore, we are requesting that additional request parameters is stored as notes on either the user or client session when processing a client grant type request in order to enable RAR for client grant tokens via a custom protocol mapper.

 Motivation

Among others, EU digital wallet framework (ARF) uses Cloud Signature Consortium (CSC) API v2, which requires the use of RAR.

Furthermore, the Japanese government agency Digital Agency is standardizing based on CSC v2, meaning they are also closely following eiDAS 2 and ARF.

While it is our impression that Keycloak will eventually fully support RAR per default, this feature request would enable RAR compatibility via a custom protocol mapper in the meantime.

 Details

My implementation idea would be to add something similar to AuthorizationEndpoint.javaL332 here: ClientCredentialsGrantType.javaL130

It would perhaps need a similar method to extractAdditionalReqParams, in order not to store all the formParams but only the "additional" parameters.
kept_issues.body:
### Description

Since Keycloak is not yet supporting [Rich Authorization Request (RAR)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9396), we are using a custom protocol mapper in order to include `authorization_details` in issued tokens, when using a [Pushed Authorization Request (PAR)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9126) flow. This was also recommended in [discussions/22991](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/22991).
This is possible because the [ParEndpoint](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/par/endpoints/ParEndpoint.java) processing goes through [AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332), that stores any additional request parameters in client session notes, which can then be accessed from a custom protocol mapper.

However, we also need RAR for a client grant type token. But since the [TokenEndpoint](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/TokenEndpoint.java) processing does not store the additional request parameters, we cannot use the custom protocol mapper to achieve RAR in this case.

Therefore, we are requesting that additional request parameters is stored as notes on either the user or client session when processing a client grant type request in order to enable RAR for client grant tokens via a custom protocol mapper.

### Motivation

Among others, [EU digital wallet framework (ARF)](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/main/docs/arf.md) uses [Cloud Signature Consortium (CSC) API v2](https://cloudsignatureconsortium.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/csc-api-v2.0.0.2.pdf), which requires the use of [RAR](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9396).

Furthermore, the Japanese government agency [Digital Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Agency) is standardizing based on CSC v2, meaning they are also closely following eiDAS 2 and ARF.

While it is our impression that Keycloak will eventually fully support RAR per default, this feature request would enable RAR compatibility via a custom protocol mapper in the meantime.

### Details

My implementation idea would be to add something similar to [AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332) here: [ClientCredentialsGrantType.java#L130](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantType.java#L130)

It would perhaps need a similar method to [extractAdditionalReqParams](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/request/AuthzEndpointRequestParser.java#L127), in order not to store all the `formParams` but only the "additional" parameters.
kept_issues.title: Enabling authorization_details for client grant tokens until RAR is fully implemented

Red Hat build of Keycloak 24

The customer would like to know if there is a possibility to consider backward compatibility to previous behavior.

Just for the backwards compatibility. kept_issues.body:
### Description

The customer has a business requirement to take certain actions if users are not configured for 2FA. They are looking to perform an authentication Flow that uses this condition to detect if a user does not have any 2FA method.

### Possible solution

The easiest approach is to implement the option `Negate output` in the condition `Condition - User configured` . The option `Negate output` is available for example in the `Condition - user role` .

Currently the `Condition - User configured` evaluates to true if at least one of the 2-factor authenticators configured in the related conditional subflow is present. So when added `Negate output` option, it will allow to have subflow, which will evaluate to true just if NONE of the configured 2-factor authenticators from the same subflow is present.

Together with the `Deny Access` authenticator, this can be used to achieve the requirement. As for example it may be possible to configure the authentication flow with the subflows like these:

```
- (All other authenticators like cookie, password etc)
- Subflow1 - 2factor enabled
  - Condition - user configured (Negate output = false)
  - OTP ALTERNATIVE
  - WebAuthn ALTERNATIVE
  - Recovery codes ALTERNATIVE
- Subflow2 - 2factor disabled
  - Condition - user configured (Negate output = true)
  - Deny Access ALTERNATIVE
  - OTP ALTERNATIVE
  - WebAuthn ALTERNATIVE
  - Recovery codes ALTERNATIVE 
```

This will allow to authenticate users with 2-factor configured (subflow1), but reject authentication for users without 2-factor configured (subflow2).

It is possible that some other adjustements may be needed in the implementation of `ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator` to make this happen or configure the `subflow2` in slightly different way. But hopefully some setup like this may work. Will need further investigation...

The disadvantage is the need of duplication of all the 2-factor authenticators in both subflows and the complication of such a setup. The better will be to have authentication policies, which would allow better achieve something like this more easily. But that is for the future though...

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_

### Details

_No response_
kept_issues.title: Ability to reject authentication to users without 2FA configured

The aim of this task is to improve support for configuring permissions for token exchange.

Currently it is possible to configure with fine-grained admin permissions that client client-a is able to exchange token with the audience target . 

It will be good to have also those abilities, which are not supported right now.
- Restrict based on scopes (EG. token exchange is permitted just if scopes scope-a or scope-b is requested, but not scope-c)
- Restrict based on token types (EG. token exchange allowed just if access token requested, but not when refresh-token requested)
- based on types of requester or target client (allow/not-allow for public clients)
- based on whether it is client has consent required
- based on whether "delegation" is needed
- More?

Right now, it is possible to configure policies on target/audience client side (EG. Group of clients, which is able to pass authorization policy X is able to exchange for audience target), but it is not possible to exchange on "requester" client side (EG. group of target clients, which can pass authorization policy Y can be exchanged as audience from requester client client-a).

 Notes

- This task might be probably divided into multiple subtasks and multiple PRs. Just using this as "umbrella" for now. Maybe converted to epic?

- Some use-cases for permissions are described in this document

- We may need to add some additional data to be available to authorization policies. Some additional attributes (like TokenExchangeContext, parsed tokens etc) can be added to EvaluationContext somewhere here

- Not 100% sure if we need 2 calls for authorization-services (one for check target client as it is now and another for check requester client like client-a), but not 100% sure yet... The check for "requester" client is possibly not strictly needed in 26.2, but could be added as a follow-up (TBD)

- There will be new admin UI and configuration for fine-grained admin permissions. This is being done by core-iam and UI teams and it is not part of this task.

- New implementation of some authorization policies may be needed. Question here is, if we can have single implementation (like TokenExchangeAuthorizationPolicy) with all the configuration on the single place like on the picture below or if we want dedicated policy implementations for various things (scopes, requested token types, consent etc) and then "aggregate" them. IMO single implementation might be better and easier for administrators to configure for token-exchange, but might be subject for discussions...
kept_issues.body:
The aim of this task is to improve support for configuring permissions for token exchange.

Currently it is possible to configure with fine-grained admin permissions that client `client-a` is able to exchange token with the audience `target` . 

It will be good to have also those abilities, which are not supported right now.
- Restrict based on scopes (EG. token exchange is permitted just if scopes `scope-a` or `scope-b` is requested, but not `scope-c`)
- Restrict based on token types (EG. token exchange allowed just if access token requested, but not when refresh-token requested)
- based on types of requester or target client (allow/not-allow for public clients)
- based on whether it is client has consent required
- based on whether "delegation" is needed
- More?

Right now, it is possible to configure policies on target/audience client side (EG. Group of clients, which is able to pass authorization policy `X` is able to exchange for audience `target`), but it is not possible to exchange on "requester" client side (EG. group of target clients, which can pass authorization policy `Y` can be exchanged as audience from requester client `client-a`).


### Notes

- This task might be probably divided into multiple subtasks and multiple PRs. Just using this as "umbrella" for now. Maybe converted to epic?

- Some use-cases for permissions are described in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T_4hjf0tapLAC5Hpac8wNiEHcrAmYZDQGpj3JRJ2MBI/edit?tab=t.0)

- We may need to add some additional data to be available to authorization policies. Some additional attributes (like `TokenExchangeContext`, parsed tokens etc) can be added to `EvaluationContext` somewhere [here](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.0.6/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissions.java#L365)

- Not 100% sure if we need 2 calls for authorization-services (one for check `target` client as it is now and another for check requester client like `client-a`), but not 100% sure yet... The check for "requester" client is possibly not strictly needed in 26.2, but could be added as a follow-up (TBD)

- There will be new admin UI and configuration for fine-grained admin permissions. This is being done by core-iam and UI teams and it is not part of this task.

- New implementation of some authorization policies may be needed. Question here is, if we can have single implementation (like `TokenExchangeAuthorizationPolicy`) with all the configuration on the single place like on the picture below or if we want dedicated policy implementations for various things (scopes, requested token types, consent etc) and then "aggregate" them. IMO single implementation might be better and easier for administrators to configure for token-exchange, but might be subject for discussions...

![Screenshot from 2024-11-28 11-52-35](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e67ad89-eaa9-4c6a-8a70-4b4dbbb13427)

Description

Current Behavior:
When a user is required to verify their email (e.g., during registration or through an admin-triggered action), the system displays a message stating that a verification email has been sent. After the email is verified, the user remains on the same page, and no further action is taken automatically.

Currently, an automatic redirect after verification is only possible via the REST API, specifically using the execute-actions-email method in the UsersResource, where a redirectUri can be defined. This is not configurable through the Admin UI.

Proposed Enhancement:
Enable configuration in the Admin UI to specify a redirect URL that users will be automatically directed to upon successful email verification. This configuration should work seamlessly with email verification triggered by both user actions and admin actions.

 Discussion

_No response_

 Motivation

Benefits:
Improved user experience by eliminating manual navigation after email verification.
Reduced friction in workflows requiring email verification.
Alignment of behavior across different verification initiation methods (Admin UI and REST API).
Implementation Suggestion:
Add a field in the Admin UI under Email Settings or Required Actions to define the redirectUri.
Ensure that this redirect is triggered universally after successful email verification, whether initiated from user registration or admin-triggered actions.
The redirectUri setting should override the default behavior and only apply if explicitly defined.
References:
Existing API behavior: The redirectUri functionality is documented under the execute-actions-email method in the UsersResource of the Keycloak Admin REST API.

### Description

Current Behavior:
When a user is required to verify their email (e.g., during registration or through an admin-triggered action), the system displays a message stating that a verification email has been sent. After the email is verified, the user remains on the same page, and no further action is taken automatically.

Currently, an automatic redirect after verification is only possible via the REST API, specifically using the execute-actions-email method in the UsersResource, where a redirectUri can be defined. This is not configurable through the Admin UI.

Proposed Enhancement:
Enable configuration in the Admin UI to specify a redirect URL that users will be automatically directed to upon successful email verification. This configuration should work seamlessly with email verification triggered by both user actions and admin actions.



### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Benefits:
Improved user experience by eliminating manual navigation after email verification.
Reduced friction in workflows requiring email verification.
Alignment of behavior across different verification initiation methods (Admin UI and REST API).
Implementation Suggestion:
Add a field in the Admin UI under Email Settings or Required Actions to define the redirectUri.
Ensure that this redirect is triggered universally after successful email verification, whether initiated from user registration or admin-triggered actions.
The redirectUri setting should override the default behavior and only apply if explicitly defined.
References:
Existing API behavior: The redirectUri functionality is documented under the execute-actions-email method in the UsersResource of the Keycloak Admin REST API.

I am not a coder, but as its possible via rest Api, Adding a additional option for the client shouldnt be problematic, but I may be totally wrong... :)

Description

Keycloak does not currently provide any mechanisms to automatically disable or remove users. There are a number of use-cases where this is relevant:

 Automatically disable dormant users
 Automatically delete abandoned users
 Transient/temporary users brokered from identity providers
 Transient/temporary users federated through user federation providers

This is relevant to PIP (for example GDPR) where it is generally a requirement to not store user information when not needed.

This is an alternative proposal to transient users for brokering. Transient users stored in sessions is not a solution to privacy for many reasons; sessions may still be persisted to the database, they may be long lived; and additionally and probably the biggest issue from a privacy perspective there is no mechanism to identity user information stored in transient user sessions, so there may be long-lived and persisted sessions storing information about users. From a privacy perspective users have the right to know what information is stored about them, as well as a right to have their information deleted from a provider; neither of which can be guaranteed with transient user sessions.

 Value Proposition
Automatically disabling and/or deletion of user accounts provides increased security (unused and no longer maintained accounts can be abused) and privacy (not storing user information when no longer needed).

 Goals
 Ability to automatically disable unused users after a configurable time
 Ability to automatically delete unused users after a configurable time
 Ability to automatically delete users from a identity provider where there are no active sessions
 Ability to automatically delete users from a federation provider where there are no active sessions
 Remove experimental transient user stored in user sessions

 Non-Goals
 Not importing users coming from an identity provider into LDAP. Ability to selectively add users to a federation provider is not covered by this issue, and would be a separate RFE.
